units.function: Unit tests for capability-gated plugin telemetry forwarding with host-added plugin namespace and restricted event-name syntax.
units.dependencyDirection: A plugin RPC handler with declared capabilities calls host telemetry services; the host prefixes the plugin key and forwards plugin-provided dimensions into the process-global telemetry client.
units.keyDataModels: Plugin ID/key; telemetry.track capability; lowercase slug eventName; arbitrary dimensions map; namespaced dynamic event; stable CAPABILITY_DENIED RPC error.
units.lifecycle: Check capability; validate event-name syntax; add plugin namespace; obtain global telemetry client; forward dimensions.
units.testAssessment: All four tests pass. Namespace prefixing, a narrow event-name grammar and explicit capability denial are sound baseline controls. The actual data boundary remains open: dimensions are arbitrary and forwarded unchanged, with no registered schema, type/field/size/cardinality/rate limits, PII/secret scanning, tenant/run attribution, consent, sink locality, backpressure or failure semantics.
units.designRationale: Let plugins contribute product telemetry without colliding with first-party event names while requiring an explicit manifest capability.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs observable extensions across managed-cloud and self-hosted enterprises without exporting employee, Agent, prompt, evidence, credential or customer data through free-form telemetry.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT namespace and capability gating only. Require each telemetry event to be registered in a signed manifest with versioned, typed, low-cardinality dimension allowlist and classification. Inject trusted plugin/version/deployment profile locally; never accept tenant/principal/run attribution from plugin fields. Reject unknown/high-cardinality or content-bearing values, secrets and identifiers by policy; enforce size/rate budgets and local aggregation. Self-hosted defaults to local/no external sink, with explicit enterprise opt-in, regional routing, retention/deletion controls and audit of export configuration.
units.responsibilityConflict: Free-form telemetry can silently export data produced by humans or Agents outside the work's data authorization contract, leaving no accountable approver or evidence of what was disclosed.

units.securityFindings: POSITIVE: explicit telemetry capability, plugin namespace and constrained event-name grammar reduce accidental collision; missing capability returns a stable RPC code. CRITICAL data-export gap for Company OS: arbitrary dimensions are forwarded to a global telemetry client without classification or redaction. HIGH privacy/locality gap: no tenant consent, self-hosted opt-out, residency, retention or deletion controls. HIGH abuse gap: no size, rate or high-cardinality budget. MEDIUM attribution gap: trusted plugin version/profile is not demonstrated and plugin dimensions could claim misleading source fields. MEDIUM resilience gap: sink failure, buffering/backpressure and offline behavior are untested.
